messages:
Alex: Nightdash alert -> p95 token-latency up ~30% across canary and prod since the 22:00 merge. Dashboard: https://dash.internal/redwood/runtime/nightly (see 'tail-latency' graph). Anyone already looking?
Maria: On it. Saw the spike around 22:03. Which rollout went out at 21:58? @Ryan? :eyes:
Ryan: That was the runtime merge: PR 3456 (batching heuristics refactor) + a small kernel-selection tweak in 3459. I rolled the staging canary at 21:50 and prod at 21:58.
Sam: CI perf bot flagged a regression on the merge pipeline: "nightly-perf-check failed: p95 increase 28%". Full CI note: ci-bot: build/3456/nightly -> perf-failure.
ci-bot: [automated] Perf regression detected for merge commit 3f8a7b2 (PR 3456). Checkpoint: nightly/p95 tokens = 124ms -> 160ms (regression threshold exceeded).
Maria: Can we bisect between 3f8a7b2 (batching refactor) and 7c2d1a0 (kernel tweak)? Start with reverting the batching change in a canary?
Alex: Before revert, quick profiling: Sam, can you run the lightweight flame/trace on a sampled request that hit high tail? Kernel selection logs + batch composition needed.
Sam: Running now on a repro trace from 22:04. Snippet from runtime logs: ```[22:03:58] request id=rc-9a3, selected_kernel=merge-stride-v2, batch_size=1, prefetch_hits=0, kv-hit=false, kv-load-ms=12.4, exec-ms=142```
Sam: Notable: batch_size frequently 1 for long tails, but exec-ms jumped when selected_kernel=merge-stride-v2. Older kernel (stride-v1) had steady lower exec-ms in replay.
Ryan: The selector change in 3459 adds a confidence-weighted switch to merge-stride-v2 for short sequences; maybe it's misclassifying and forcing heavier kernel. I can flip selector to prefer stride-v1 in canary to test.
Maria: Also noticed KV eviction pressure around same timeframe in the cache metrics. KV evictions spiked 2x at 22:02 -> could explain low prefetch_hits. Link: https://dash.internal/redwood/kv/evictions/nightly
Alex: So two hypotheses: (A) selector misrouting to heavier kernel for many short requests; (B) KV coldness evictions causing more backend work and magnifying kernel cost. Prioritize quick mitigations.
Ryan: I'm going to patch selector in canary to force stride-v1 for sequences <=64 tokens. Pushing patch now (canary rollout 10%). Commit: 8b9c4d1.
ci-bot: [automated] Canary rollout started for runtime: commit 8b9c4d1 -> traffic 10% at 22:15
Sam: Ran replay against canary patch locally — p95 drops back to ~126ms in repro traces. Good signal.
Maria: If canary holds at 10% for 15m, we should promote to 50% then full. Also spike in KV evictions needs a follow-up: increase cache size for a night to observe effect.
Alex: Agreed. Hold the main rollout until canary at 50% is stable or we do a rollback. @Ryan monitor tail and kv metrics; Sam run a few more replay permutations (vary seq len + batch concurrency).
Ryan: Monitoring now. Early signal: tail at 10% traffic improved ~18%; kv evictions unchanged.
Sam: Replay matrix in progress. Adding logs for kernel selection decisions and batch-formation reasons (why batch_size=1 kept). I'll add a temporary trace flag to capture decision paths.
Maria: I'll open a follow-up issue to revert the batching-refactor if we see other regressions after selector tweak. Issue: INF-1209.
Alex: Temp rollout-block in place for next deploy until 50% canary confirms. Marking release as "on-hold". Thanks all, keep updates short in this thread. :thumbsup:
